title: _process() "catches up" after pause-unpause
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.7) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M2 - Apple M2 (8 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

_(Apologies if this is a duplicate, I searched but didn't find anything. Also sorry if I'm doing this wrong.. It's my first time, and I tried checking in Discord first [(here)](https://discord.com/channels/1235157165589794909/1334482804863406101/1530753050791252049), but got no replies.)_

When I use the pause button, things pause, but when I unpause, everything goes *SUPER FAST*, ie all the `_process()` calls happen rapidly at once, like it's trying to "catch up"

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1f1b702-a816-4301-89f3-b74470f74f8b

Here's a video showing it happening with a simple print count: you can see I try to visually bounce the mouse cursor roughly every second (about 100 counts), but when I click resume, there's a huge surge in the number of `_process()` calls, catching up as if it were never paused at all.
What this looks like with actual game logic happening in process calls is: after unpause, everything goes _crazy fast_ until it makes up for the lost time while paused.

I don't believe this is intentional behavior? Apologies if that is incorrect.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the attached project _(notice the godot icon slowly slide across the screen at a set rate)_
3. Pause _(notice it stops moving)_
4. Wait a bit
5. Resume _(notice it moves crazy fast, until it catches up to where it would have been, then resumes its original speed))_

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[process_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30879808/process_bug.zip)

To make this, I just created a new project, dragged the icon into the scene, and gave it a script with `position += Vector2(1, 0)` inside `_process()`

Here's a new video showing the MRP:
 
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40078f67-ea84-431b-8ba3-6b22abeae89e
